merger_name: SAS Trustee Corporation – Australia Pacific Airport Corporation
merger_description:
SAS Trustee Corporation (**STC**) is the trustee of the New South Wales State Superannuation Scheme, constituted by the *State Authorities Superannuation Act 1987* (NSW) and acts as an institutional investor, investing in a diversified portfolio of assets. STC currently holds an 18.47% interest in the Australia Pacific Airport Corporation (**APAC**), which holds long-term leases to own and operate Melbourne Airport (Victoria) and Launceston Airport (Tasmania).

Following a decision of the Supreme Court of New South Wales in May 2026, the APAC shares held by Dexus Capital Investment Services Pty Ltd are to be divested in accordance with the process contained in the Shareholders’ Deed which makes the shares available to existing, non-defaulting shareholders (including STC) under a pre-emptive share acquisition regime. By way of this process, STC proposes to acquire additional shares in APAC.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition. In particular:
a. STC already holds an interest in APAC, and the Acquisition
does not create any new horizontal overlap between STC
and APAC in the supply of airport infrastructure and related
services in Australia
b. other than STC’s existing interest in APAC, there is no
horizontal overlap between STC’s portfolio and APAC in the
supply of airport infrastructure and related services in
Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
